title: C¹ Approximation Theorem for real Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Lipschitz with constant K ≥ 0 (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there exist a closed set A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε (Lⁿ = volume, Lebesgue measure) and a C¹ function h : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that for every x ∈ A: g(x) = h(x), and g is Fréchet differentiable at x with derivative Dh(x) (so ∇g(x) = ∇h(x)).
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (g : Eucl n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K g → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ (A : Set (Eucl n)) (h : Eucl n → ℝ), IsClosed A ∧ (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) Aᶜ < ε ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 h ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, g x = h x ∧ HasFDerivAt g (fderiv ℝ h x) x
